logline: A Joseon-era crown prince time-travels 300 years to modern Seoul after his wife's mysterious death, assuming a contemporary billionaire's identity while investigating whether history is about to repeat itself.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb rates it 7.7/10, with MyDramaList audience giving high scores for the inventive fish-out-of-water comedy setup and Park Yoo-chun's committed physical performance as the bewildered Joseon prince.

seasons.review_body: Rooftop Prince aired on SBS in spring 2012, averaging 12.1 percent nationwide by the TNmS metric - solid for a time-travel romantic comedy competing in a crowded primetime slot. The drama won a devoted international following, particularly in China and Japan, with fans from over 35 countries visiting filming locations. The premise is genuinely inventive: a grieving prince displaced in time, surrounded by three loyal retainers equally baffled by modern Seoul, navigating a reincarnation mystery that doubles as a corporate thriller. Early episodes mine this setup for sharp physical comedy. The second half shifts register toward melodrama and the tonal gear-change divides opinion - MyDramaList reviews praise the first-half charm, while several note the finale's emotional logic as undercooked. Park Yoo-chun's earnest commitment to the slapstick keeps the whole construct credible.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Joseon cold-open is shot with enough period atmosphere to make the time-travel rupture genuinely jarring - the four men landing on a Seoul rooftop is staged as pure disorientation comedy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The crown prince's first encounter with a smartphone - played with complete bewildered sincerity.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 20
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the reincarnation mystery with emotional ambition that somewhat outpaces its own plotting - affecting in moments but less airtight than the premise promised.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final resolution of the who-killed-the-crown-princess thread, which recontextualizes both timelines.
